title.narrative: Strengthening markets, Productive Alliances and financial services in Rural communities (SPARK)

description.narrative: Objective 1: Create or improve alliances between MSME agribusiness and other key actors within value chainsObjective 2: Improved primary processing and irrigation capacity in key value chainsObjective 3: Increase access to and use of financing by MSME agribusinesses

The SPARK programme will provide a package of support to enable MSME agri-business in Gedaref and Kassala states to recover from the current crisis. The package of assistance aims to meet a range of MSMEs’ needs in a holistic and interconnected way. To support integration and concentration of benefits, SPARK will utilise a cluster-based development approach. The cluster approach enables smallholder farmers and MSME agro-businesses to engage in high-value agriculture through several key mechanisms.Through the programme, Mercy Corps will establish a number of SPARK hubs to act as centres for aggregation, processing and distribution of agricultural products from the surrounding smallholder farmers. The hubs will also provide an important conduit for linkages between smallholder farmers / MSMEs and bigger lead companies (such as secondary processors, wholesalers, big retailers, and institutions). By strengthening these linkages through the hubs, the programme aims to boost the income smallholder farmers receive, increase productivity, and support rural employment opportunities. The SPARK hubs will support the development of new productive alliances through the provision of Business Development Services for MSMEs and promote linkages with lead firms. Solar technology will be deployed to support the efficient and sustainable primary processing of agricultural commodities. Year-round cultivation will be supported through solar irrigation. MSMEs will also have improved access to finance through the co-design of new financial products and services with partner Financial Service Providers (FSPs) to aid recovery. This will include the establishment of a revolving loan fund tailored to the needs of MSME agri-businesses who continue to face challenges with access to finance.

title.narrative: Objective 1: Create or improve alliances between MSME agribusiness and other key actors within value chains
# of MSMEs gaining new or improved access to the value chain

description.narrative: •Tracks the number of MSMEs that newly or improve access value chain.•A value chain describes the full range of activities that are required to bring a product or service from conception, through the intermediary phases of production and delivery to final consumers, and final disposal after use. The term value chain is usually used with a developmental connotation addressing productivity, growth and job creation in the market system.•New access: new participation in a specific value chain•Improve access: continued and improved participation in a specific value chain

title.narrative: Output 1.1: Strengthen upstream value chain linkages between MSMEs and smallholder farmers / producer associations
# of MSMEs that utilize the business development services

description.narrative: This indicator counts the number MSMEs that participated in BDS training service that are utilizing the skills learnt in running of their business activities.•BDS refers to range of training and support the program intends to render to participating MSMEs.This training includes the following:•Business planning and management: to improve business planning skills, increase knowledge on entrepreneurship, strategic thinking, business relations to meet goals, and financial projections.•Marketing: deepen marketing skills, branding, advertising, and customer service. •Financial literacy: strengthen financial planning, management, and bookkeeping skills.•Organisational development and financing: strengthen the managerial capacity of existing and especially newly established MSMEs.•Advocacy: to improve the ability of entrepreneurs to be in a stronger position to lobby and advocate for a favourable ecosystem for MSME / agricultural enterprises within their local areas. •Leadership skills: including leadership development, networking, and negotiating with financial institutions

title.narrative: Objective 3: Increase access to and use of financing by MSME agribusinesses
# of MSMEs that obtain financial services

description.narrative: •Total number of MSMEs obtaining or obtaining financial services of any type as a result of the intervention. (example the Agri-business Recovery Fund ARF)•Financial services can include loans and other forms of credit (e.g., trade finance, leasing credit), savings/deposit accounts, transfers, or insurance products (e.g. weather insurance), card products (e.g. debit, credit, prepaid, or other), credit or financial counselling, micro leasing, mobile banking services, payment services (e.g. by check, payroll cards, or other), remittance services, savings facilitation services, scholarship or educational grants, or others.•Obtained : In order to be counted, the MSME must have acquired/receivedthe service and not just applied for it.

title.narrative: Output 1.2: Strengthen downstream value chain linkages between MSMEs and larger buyers / retailers and processors
Average compound annual growth rate of supported MSMEs

description.narrative: • This indicator measures the average rate of growth in revenue, employment, or assets of MSMEs that have received support (e.g., financing, training, mentorship) throught the program life cycle.Growth Rate = (End Value / Beginning Value)^(1/Number of Years) - 1Average CAGR = (∑(Growth Rate of each MSME)) / Number of MSMEsA higher average CAGR indicates that supported MSMEs are growing at a faster rate, suggesting effective support mechanisms. A negative CAGR indicates decline or stagnation
